Calculate the gap between take-home income and spending.
Cash flow describes money moving in and out during a specific period. Use take-home income, because
payroll deductions are already gone. Add spending for the same period, then subtract it from income. A
positive difference is room to allocate; a negative one signals a gap to address.
A monthly surplus can hide a timing problem. Rent might arrive before a paycheck. Keep a bill calendar
alongside the monthly total. Borrowed money can temporarily raise a bank balance, but it is not earned income

Grade 8 Mathematics • Real numbers and exponents
I can classify a number as rational or irrational and locate an irrational number between rational numbers.
A rational number can be written as a ratio of two integers, and its decimal form either ends or repeats a fixed block forever.
A decimal that never ends and never settles into a repeating block is irrational, so it cannot be written as a ratio of two integers.
An irrational square root can be located on a number line by trapping its radicand between the squares of nearby rational numbers.
